title: Introduction to Events in Node.js
overview: Events are actions or occurrences that happen during program execution. Node.js uses an event-driven architecture to handle asynchronous operations.

example.title: Event Examples
example.content:
✔ User request
✔ File completed loading
✔ Server started
✔ Data received

title: EventEmitter Module
overview: The EventEmitter class is provided by Node.js to create, listen, and trigger custom events.

example.title: EventEmitter Example
example.content:
const EventEmitter = require('events');

const event = new EventEmitter();

title: Creating and Listening to Events
overview: Events are created using emit() and handled using listener functions with on().

title: Understanding Event Loop
overview: The event loop manages asynchronous tasks and allows Node.js to execute non-blocking operations efficiently.

example.title: Event Loop Flow
example.content:
Call Stack
 ↓
Async APIs
 ↓
Callback Queue
 ↓
Event Loop

title: Callbacks and Event Handling
overview: Callbacks are functions passed to other functions and executed after an asynchronous operation completes.

title: Topic Summary
overview: You learned how Node.js handles events using EventEmitter, listeners, emitters, callbacks, and the event loop.

example.title: Quick Revision
example.content:
✔ Node.js is event-driven.
✔ EventEmitter creates events.
✔ emit triggers events.
✔ Event loop handles async tasks.
